citation: Douglas J. Leith, 'The Quality of Claude AI-authored Python Tests Is Not Weaker Than Human-authored Tests', arXiv:2608.15188 (cs.SE), submitted 15 August 2026. https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15188. Secondary source also opened at abstract level: Jeff Otterson, 'Adversarial Test-Hardening for AI-Written Code: An Instrument Autopsy and a Pre-Registered Causal Estimate of the Critic Loop', arXiv:2607.23002, 25 July 2026. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23002
source_tier: Preprint (arXiv, not peer-reviewed) for both. Single-author each.
access_status: Abstract page only for both papers. The PDFs were fetched but returned compressed binary the fetch tool could not read, so no body text (tables, mutation scores, limitations sections) was verified. [uncertain] for anything beyond the abstracts.
sponsor_and_incentive: Not stated on either abstract page [uncertain]. Leith's paper evaluates Claude models; no disclosure of Anthropic funding seen, but body text not read. Otterson is affiliated with W. P. Carey School of Business, Arizona State University.
exact_quotes: Leith abstract (arXiv abs page): "We evaluate the quality of Claude AI-written Python tests against human-written Python tests" / "from two established open-source projects Django and Pandas." / "Hundreds of tests per corpus are scored under one identical protocol." / "(Sonnet/Opus 4.6 and later) are no weaker than the two human-written corpora." / "every test is individually scored under three independent fault-injection protocols plus a seven-axis qualitative design rubric". Otterson: only a paraphrase of the abstract was obtained from the fetch tool, no verbatim quote available.
date_and_recency: Leith: 15 August 2026. Otterson: 25 July 2026. Both within the 12 months before 2026-10-16. Data collection windows not seen [uncertain].
key_claims: Leith: tests written by recent Claude models (Sonnet/Opus 4.6 and later) in real tool use are no weaker than human-written tests from Django and Pandas, using one-sided non-inferiority bounds and three fault-injection protocols (mutation-style) plus a design rubric. Scored per test, not per suite. Otterson (via abstract summary): a loop where a Tester model writes tests, mutation testing finds surviving mutants, and a Critic model writes tests to kill them; all verdicts mechanical. The loop killed mutants one-shot generation missed.
headline_figures: Leith: no numbers beyond 'hundreds of tests per corpus' were visible on the abstract page [uncertain]. Otterson (from abstract page, second-hand via fetch summary): Experiment 1, five Python subjects, loop killed 105 mutants that one-shot generation missed and lost none. Experiment 2 (pre-registered, four subjects, five replicates): same-lineage Critic rounds killed 78% of surviving mutants (mean 0.783, 95% cluster-bootstrap CI [0.592, 0.935]). Cross-provider pilot gap 0.178 (CI [0.039, 0.347]), magnitude dominated by one replicate. An earlier reported p = 9.5e-66 cross-lineage effect was an instrument artifact (output truncation).
sample_unit_and_population: Leith: individual tests; open-source Django and Pandas; hundreds of tests per corpus; Python only; Claude models only. Otterson: five Python subjects (Exp 1), four subjects (Exp 2); small, likely synthetic or small-project subjects [uncertain].
observed_vs_stated: Observed: tests were executed under fault injection / mutation, mechanical outcomes. Not self-reported belief.
what_makes_trust_justified: Mutation or fault-injection scoring of each test, rather than line coverage, as an independent mechanical check on whether tests detect defects. Otterson adds a mutation-driven critic loop that adds tests to kill survivors, with no model judging another model.
what_it_costs: Not quantified in the abstracts [uncertain]. Otterson mentions a cross-provider arm costing 5.5x less than the other, but total loop cost was not seen. Mutation testing generally adds compute time; not verified here.
failure_mode_class: Wrong or weak code verification (tests that pass but do not detect faults); over-reliance on coverage as a proxy.
control_that_would_have_prevented: Not an incident study. Applicable control: run mutation testing on agent-written tests and require surviving mutants to be killed before accepting the tests.
limitations_stated: Leith: none visible on abstract page; scope is two projects and Claude 4.6+ models only (this is the abstract's own scope, not a stated caveat). Otterson (from fetch summary): cross-provider comparison confounded by harness and truncation failures; pilot driven by a single replicate; one Exp 1 cell could not be scored; only four or five subjects.
counter_evidence: Leith's result cuts against the premise that agent-written tests are weaker than human ones: Claude tests were found no weaker than the human corpora. The paper does not, from the abstract, show mutation score revealing weakness that coverage hides. Otterson shows one-shot AI tests leave killable mutants, which supports the premise, but only in a small Python sample. Background (older than 12 months, search-snippet only, not opened): arXiv 2506.02954 reports LLM suites with 100% coverage killing about 4% of mutants; arXiv 2501.12862 (Meta ACH).
verification_status: Existence, authorship, dates and abstract wording of both papers: checked against arXiv abstract pages actually opened. All numeric results for Otterson: abstract-level summary only, full text not read [uncertain]. Leith's mutation scores: not seen [uncertain]. Background papers 2506.02954 and 2501.12862: search snippets only, not opened [uncertain]. Property-based testing: no qualifying source found; dropped that half of the topic.
usable_claim: A 2026 preprint (Leith, arXiv:2608.15188) scored hundreds of Claude-written tests against human-written tests from Django and Pandas under fault injection and found the Claude tests no weaker. Another 2026 preprint (Otterson, arXiv:2607.23002) reports that a mutation-driven critic loop killed mutants that one-shot AI-written tests had missed. Both are preprints; the essay should not claim mutation testing is proven to expose weak agent tests at scale.
do_not_use: The 78% kill rate, the 105 mutants and the p-value as essay figures (only seen second-hand, small sample, preprint). Any claim that coverage hides weak agent tests based on Leith (his result is the opposite). The 4% mutants-killed and 15-25% figures from search snippets and blogs. Any property-based testing claim.
overlap_with_existing_essays: Not checked against the Verification Gap or Checking Isn't Catching essays [uncertain]. Not verified whether they use either paper.
